Fixed sequence: sleeping Quixote; niece supplies library keys; housekeeper requests holy water; priest and barber examine books; Amadís defended and spared for now; Esplandián condemned; selective praise and rejection; Palmerín of England reprieved; Tirant accidentally falls from housekeeper’s bundle and is singled out; pastoral/poetry debate, Diana editing proposal; Galatea receives mixed judgement; heroic poetry praised; scrutiny interrupted by Quixote’s imagined tournament; household returns him to bed; food and sleep; remaining books burned that night, including unexamined worthy works; entrance walled and plastered; two days later missing-room search; household invents magician, Quixote identifies Fristón; niece’s warning angers him; fifteen quiet days with arguments; Sancho persuaded by promise of island; money raised through poor bargains, borrowed shield and repaired helmet, shirts and saddlebags; donkey permitted; secret night departure without family farewells; morning talk expands island to kingdom and family titles. Stop at the end of I.7, before windmills.

The chapter-6 catalogue is selectively condensed, not replaced by a simple claim that all books are equally condemned. Judgements concern literary merit, taste, influence, friendship and feared effects on Quixote. A reprieve in the scrutiny is not a guarantee that every reprieved volume survives the later indiscriminate burning. Tirant’s praise and the contradictory galleys remark are both retained. Several lesser catalogue entries are summarized. Sancho’s wife’s inconsistent names in this passage are avoided by saying his wife; his dismissive ranking is presented as his opinion, not fact.

All dialogue is original modern adaptation, with no direct-source quotation labels. Student helper, record of judgements, journal, local questions and NPC replies are invented connective material. The priest/barber make the verdicts and the household performs the confinement; Sancho’s canonical choice to join is not given to the student. Seven binary choices affect conversation and bounded callbacks, not the fixed source events.

Visuals are theatrical: library background is shown during scrutiny; the original courtyard is the home-side viewpoint for the unseen bedroom; a new matching courtyard shows the entrance plastered over after the removal. The journal provides the intervening night/time transition. Other time-of-day changes remain narrated on a continuous theatrical set. Books in hand, holy water, fire, masonry, armour and animals are narrated/mimed. No book-burning spectacle or unsafe student participation. The cartoon cast uses common proportions rather than literal physical likenesses. Quixote’s visible lance on the second journey anticipates the lance explicitly present in I.8; I.7 does not specify its replacement. No windmill event is imported.
